newsitem.title: JAPAN: Almaz says to resume PGM exports at 'nearest' time.
newsitem.headline: Almaz says to resume PGM exports at 'nearest' time.

text.p: Russian platinum group metal export agency Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz) said in a statement on Wednesday that Russia would resume exports of platinum group metals (PGMs) at the "nearest" possible time.
An agency official declined to comment on the exact time Russian PGM exports would resume.
The export agency also said in the statement that Almaz is still Russia's only exporter of PGMs.
Rumours had circulated that the Russian central bank would become a seller of PGMs, depriving Almaz of its monopoly.
"Almaz is still the sole exporter of PGM from Russia," it said.
Japanese traders had also been speculating that a bureaucratic hold-up was behind the protracted delay in Russian PGM exports to Japan.
Almaz said the delay was because of big changes in Russia.

The agency told Japanese clients it would resume PGM sales in the spot market in late June, and it was agreed that the agency would resume delivery to Japan under contracts around July 10, based on average PGM prices on NYMEX in the last half of June, Japanese traders said.
Although Japan-Russia export contract talks are usually held in mid-December, before the start of the new year, talks on 1997 contracts were not held until June 1-June 11 of this year.
One Japanese trade house source said the Russian agency was finally granted its PGM export licence.

"We were informed yesterday that Almaz got its export licence. Almaz can now resume sales to Japanese clients who hope to receive June delivery in the spot market in late June," a senior trader at a trading house said.
"We have signed documents for July to December delivery from Russia under long-term contracts," the trader said.
Russia supplies more than 60 percent of the world's palladium and about 20 percent of its platinum. Japan is the world's largest consumer of platinum group metals.
